limitations_and_boundaries: scGen has been trained on relatively small data sets, which only reflect subsets of biological and transcriptional variability.
A trained model cannot be expected to be predictive beyond the domain of the training data.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

research_questions.statement: Can scGen accurately predict single-cell perturbation responses for phenomena absent from training data?

provenance.text_excerpt: scGen accurately models perturbation and infection response of cells across cell types, studies and species.

claims.statement: scGen accurately predicts single-cell perturbation response out-of-sample across cell types, studies, and species.

experiments_or_tasks: Predict IFN-β stimulation response in PBMC cell types held out during training using scGen, compared to other models.

methods.name: scGen model
methods.protocol_description: scGen combines a variational autoencoder (VAE) with latent space vector arithmetics to predict perturbation response. The VAE models P(x_i|z_i, p_i) and vector arithmetics models dependence on perturbation condition p_i. δ vector is estimated as avg(z_condition=1) - avg(z_condition=0) in latent space.
